hits.mechanism: KLA's annual report lists TSMC as a customer above 10% of its revenue, and TSMC's October revenue rose 59.7% from a year earlier. Growth at that customer is a read on demand for KLA's process control tools.
Lam names TSMC among its most significant customers, and TSMC's October revenue was 59.7% above a year earlier. The report does not say how much of that turns into new equipment orders for Lam.

NVIDIA's annual report says TSMC produces its semiconductor wafers, so TSMC's 14.7% month-on-month and 59.7% year-on-year revenue rise is a read on the foundry output behind NVIDIA's chips. TSMC does not break the figure out by customer.

AMD uses TSMC for the wafers of its HPC, FPGA and adaptive SoC products, so TSMC's 59.7% year-over-year revenue rise is a read on the capacity those products run on. The report does not show AMD's own share of it.

TSMC is Astera Labs' sole manufacturing partner, so TSMC's October figures describe the one foundry all of Astera's chips depend on. Total foundry revenue up 59.7% does not show whether Astera's own volumes grew.

Credo used TSMC exclusively for wafer production in fiscal 2026, which ties it closely to the foundry's output and capacity. TSMC's 59.7% year-over-year revenue rise is an industry-wide figure, not a measure of Credo's orders.

Intel buys TSMC capacity for some tiles and products and also names TSMC its primary competitor in leading-edge process technology. A 59.7% year-over-year revenue rise at TSMC reads one way for Intel the customer and the other way for Intel's foundry business.
Cirrus Logic has most of its wafers made at TSMC, but TSMC's total monthly revenue says little about Cirrus Logic's own volumes.
Silicon Labs has most of its wafers made at TSMC and SMIC, but TSMC's total monthly revenue says little about Silicon Labs' own volumes.
Analog Devices sources part of its wafers from foundries such as TSMC, too small a link for TSMC's total revenue to describe its business.
Allegro uses TSMC as one of several fab partners, too small a link for TSMC's total revenue to describe its business.
The quoted Broadcom link is about assembly and test contractors, which TSMC's monthly revenue figure does not describe.
The path runs through Intel's own fabs, which TSMC's revenue report does not describe.
GlobalFoundries supplies AMD at other nodes; TSMC's revenue report does not describe that business.
The path from TSMC through AMD's processors to Hewlett Packard Enterprise is too long for a monthly foundry revenue figure to carry.

Amkor names ASE Technology among the main packaging and test providers it competes with. ASE's October revenue, up 47.1% from a year earlier, is a read on demand for the outsourced assembly and test services both companies sell.

ASE performs most of Lattice's wafer sort testing, so ASE's 47.1% year-over-year revenue rise describes a test base Lattice relies on. The figure covers all of ASE's customers, not Lattice's own volumes.
SPIL is one of several assembly and test providers for AMD; ASE's total revenue says little about AMD's business.
ASE is one of several assembly and test contractors Broadcom names; ASE's total revenue says little about Broadcom's business.
ASE is one of four assembly and test suppliers Qualcomm names; ASE's total revenue says little about Qualcomm's business.

Arrow is Microchip's largest distributor at 12% of net sales, so Microchip's 42.2% year-over-year sales growth ran partly through Arrow's components business. Microchip guides December-quarter net sales to between down 3% and up 1% sequentially.
NXP lists Microchip among its primary public competitors. Microchip's net sales rose 42.2% from a year earlier and 9.2% sequentially, a read on demand in the chip markets the two companies share.
Silicon Labs names Microchip as a competitor, and Microchip's 42.2% year-over-year sales growth is a read on demand in the markets the two share.
MACOM lists Microchip as one of eleven competitors; the release does not speak to the RF and photonic markets MACOM names.
AMD names Microsemi, a Microchip unit, as an FPGA competitor; Microchip's release does not speak to FPGAs.

The release says Texas Instruments is acquiring Silicon Labs, whose annual report also names Texas Instruments a competitor. Revenue up 22% from a year earlier and EPS 23.8% above consensus describe the business Texas Instruments is set to acquire.
Silicon Labs names Microchip as a competitor, and its revenue rose 22% from a year earlier, a read on demand in the markets the two share.
Silicon Labs names NXP as a competitor, and its revenue rose 22% from a year earlier, a read on demand in the markets the two share.
Silicon Labs is a small TSMC customer; its results say little about TSMC's business.
Qualcomm is one name in a list of twelve competitors; the release does not speak to a market they share.
STMicroelectronics is one name in a list of twelve competitors; the release does not speak to a market they share.
Synaptics is one name in a list of twelve competitors; the release does not speak to a market they share.

Nova says it competes mainly with Onto Innovation and KLA in metrology and process control. Onto's record quarterly revenue, up 88% from a year earlier and above its own guidance range, is a read on demand in the market Nova sells into.

Onto names Camtek one of its principal competitors in advanced packaging inspection. Onto's revenue rose 88% from a year earlier and it expects 2026 revenue growth above 45%, a read on demand for the inspection tools both sell.

Onto names KLA a principal competitor in thin film and critical dimension metrology. Onto's 88% year-over-year revenue growth points to strong process control spending, though KLA's broader business makes the read weaker.
PDF Solutions competes with Onto only in software; the release does not speak to that business.
